sentimento.text1: With 66 days to the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), Thursday brought a national poll and it came from PoderData. PoderData/Aya of Jul 30 (n=2,400, field Jul 26 to 29, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-07845/2026, telephone on mobile and landline, 677 municipalities across the 27 states) has Lula at 41% against Flávio Bolsonaro at 35% in the first round, with Ronaldo Caiado at 5%, Renan Santos at 4%, Romeu Zema at 3% and Augusto Cury at 3%, plus 5% blank or void and 4% who did not answer. In the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), Lula 46% to Flávio 43%, a 3pp difference that fits inside the two margins added together and is therefore a statistical tie. The round also brings Lula's personal approval at 43% against 49% disapproval, government rating at 44% to 50%, and TIED rejection: 49% for Lula and 49% for Flávio.
sentimento.text2: The day's crossing repeats Jul 28 and it is what organizes the reading: the price moved a full point and the polling, read properly, is flat. Lula RISES 1.00pp and returns to 63.50%, with the gap over Flávio widening from +38.55pp to +39.55pp. The comparison that counts is PoderData against itself, and there the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) gap did NOT move: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% to 34%) and it is 6pp now (41% to 35%), with the top two each gaining 1pp, inside the 2pp margin. The tightening only shows up if the ruler is swapped mid-measurement, comparing today's PoderData with yesterday's AtlasIntel, which gave 9.1pp. That is a house effect, not movement, and the panel does not add the two together. The temptation was to write that the polling tightened, because 6pp against yesterday's AtlasIntel 9.1pp looks like tightening. It is not. It is the same level difference between the two houses that the panel has been recording since Jul 16, when PoderData contradicted Genial/Quaest with Lula IDENTICAL in both and the whole disagreement concentrated on Flávio.
sentimento.text3: In the market, Lula rose 1.00pp and returned to 63.50% (vol USD 7.74M), a level that TIES the top of the AFOS series for the third time, set on Jul 26, Jul 28 and now Jul 30, without exceeding it on any of the three. The +39.55pp gap sits 0.25pp below the series maximum, the +39.80pp of Jul 26. Flávio was FLAT at 23.95% (vol USD 7.71M), breaking a run of four straight daily closes on the rise, and the distinction matters: the gap widened by movement on one side only, so there was no repricing of his candidacy today. Renan Santos fell 0.25pp, to 8.45% (vol USD 8.59M), below every daily close of the past week, but his movement is not in the winner book. Caiado rose 0.20pp, to 2.55% (vol USD 5.20M), adding up to 0.65pp over two sessions, from 1.90% on Jul 28. Zema fell 0.20pp, to 0.55%, Haddad fell 0.10pp, to 0.15%, and Jair stayed put at 1.05%. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market adds up to USD 116.58M.
sentimento.direita: Flávio was FLAT at 23.95% (vol USD 7.71M) and the run of four straight daily gains, which had come from 22.90% on Jul 25, stopped without a fall. The one who widened the gap today was Lula. In the sub-markets he ROSE 0.50pp in the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book, which moves to 79.00% in a contract of USD 215,000, his highest mark there in the panel's tracking, and stayed put at 6.25% in the third-place book. The counterpart to that rise is Renan Santos collapsing in the same book: the market is concentrating in Flávio the probability of taking the second [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) slot. In the polling, PoderData puts him at 35% in the first round, against 34% from the same house on Jul 16, and at 43% in the runoff, the same value as the institute's two previous rounds. The news is rejection: 49%, TIED with Lula's, when yesterday's AtlasIntel gave 52.9% against 49.4%. In every recent national poll, with the exception of Gerp on Jul 22, his rejection had come in equal to or above Lula's. One reading does not undo the series, but it is on the record. In Thursday's state polls, he leads Rio Grande do Sul in both rounds, 32% to 30% and 40% to 35%, and sits second in Goiás with 27%. The Aug 5 deadline for naming a running mate still stands.
sentimento.esquerda: Lula rose 1.00pp and returned to 63.50% (vol USD 7.74M), tying the top of the AFOS series for the third time without exceeding it. It is the third day out of seven in which the price moves a full point, and the pattern the panel keeps recording is that these moves do not coincide with movement in the polling. In Thursday's PoderData he has 41% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 46% to 43% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), and inside the house itself the first-round gap has been flat at 6pp since Jul 16. What moved in the round was not voting intention, it was evaluation: personal approval falls to 43% against 49% disapproval, and the GOVERNMENT MANAGEMENT rating gets sharply worse, with poor or terrible at 47%, up 10pp against the institute's Jul 22 round. It is the worst management number in the window, and it lands 24 hours after AtlasIntel measured approval RISING 1.7pp on the same kind of question. Two houses, two opposite signals in the same week. In Thursday's Genial/Quaest state polls, he loses Rio Grande do Sul in both rounds, wins Ceará 55% to 22% and comes THIRD in Goiás with 23%. In his own camp's calendar, the PSB formalized Alckmin as running mate on Jul 29, and the PT national convention that formalizes him is set for Aug 2, in São Paulo.
sentimento.terceiraVia: The chasing pack produced the day's most informative movement, and it is a RECLASSIFICATION of Renan Santos. In the winner book he gave up little, 0.25pp, to 8.45% (vol USD 8.59M). In the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book he COLLAPSED from 11.70% to 6.10%, a fall of 5.60pp in a contract of USD 1.09M. And in the third-place book he ROSE 0.50pp, to 62.00% in a contract of USD 164,000. Added up, the three say the same thing: the money did not take him out of the election, it took away his chance of reaching the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) and settled him into third place. And the polling went the same way. PoderData has him at 4%, against 6% from the same house on Jul 16, a 2pp fall that is the round's largest individual swing. That UNDOES yesterday's finding, when the panel recorded the distance between price and polling narrowing to 0.90pp based on AtlasIntel's 7.8%: today it REOPENS to 4.45pp. Convergence measured against a single survey is not a trend, and the spread between institutes still runs six points wide within the same month, between 7.8% and 3%. CAIADO went the other way and is the only name where price and polling rose together: 5% at PoderData, up 1pp inside the house, and 2.55% in the market (vol USD 5.20M), up 0.20pp, adding to 0.65pp over two sessions, from 1.90% on Jul 28. The divergence about him did not close and still stands at three levels: 6% at Nexus, 5% at PoderData, 3.1% at AtlasIntel. The state figure of the day is the sharpest mismatch of the round: Genial/Quaest has him LEADING Goiás with 33%, ahead of Flávio (27%) and Lula (23%), in the same survey where disapproval of his state government is 59%. ZEMA fell on both measures, from 4% to 3% in the polling and 0.20pp in the market, to 0.55%.
sentimento.polymarket: Lula 63.50% (up 1.00pp, vol USD 7.74M), Flávio 23.95% (flat, vol USD 7.71M), Renan Santos 8.45% (down 0.25pp, vol USD 8.59M), Caiado 2.55% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 5.20M), Jair 1.05% (flat), Zema 0.55% (down 0.20pp), Michelle 0.45%, Haddad 0.15% (down 0.10pp). Lula's gap over Flávio at +39.55pp, against +38.55pp on Jul 29, sitting 0.25pp below the series maximum. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 116.58M. Sub-markets: [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second place with Flávio 79.00% (up 0.50pp, vol USD 215,000) and Renan Santos 6.10% (DOWN 5.60pp, vol USD 1.09M); third place with Renan 62.00% (up 0.50pp, vol USD 164,000), Caiado 25.50% (flat, vol USD 37,000), Flávio 6.25% (flat) and Zema 4.50%; impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice at 3.10% (down 0.25pp, vol USD 83,000); Senate with PL 65.50% (DOWN 5.50pp, vol USD 258,000) and MDB 18.20% (up 0.60pp); inflation with the 5.00% to 5.49% band at 38.30%, the 4.50% to 4.99% band at 32.50% (down 2.40pp) and the 5.50% to 5.99% band at 5.80% (up 1.70pp). The double-reading capture guard ran once and APPROVED with no divergence at all across the five books it covers, which had not happened since Jul 28: it blocked on both of the previous rounds. Every price goes in FIRM, with no declared range. Live capture Jul 30, 20:08 UTC.

inss.text1: The fiscal agenda entered a fourth day with no fresh development: the Senate in recess, priority bills stalled and the promulgation of the [pauta-bomba](/en/glossary#pauta-bomba) still held back by Davi Alcolumbre, with the Budget as the next front of friction between the Senate presidency and the government. The day's economic axis came from abroad and by statement, not by measure: Lula said nobody is going to stick their nose into Brazil's elections, a criticism aimed at the United States and Argentina, and the government kept treating the extension of the American national emergency over Brazil, signed on Jul 28, as possible preparation for new sanctions. No new measure was announced on Thursday, and the panel records the absence.
inss.text2: The market did today what it had already done on Jul 28, and the repetition is more informative than the move on its own. The favourite's price rose 1.00pp, to 63.50%, and the day's polling, read inside the house itself, is flat. The comparison that counts is PoderData against itself, and there the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) gap did NOT move: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% to 34%) and it is 6pp now (41% to 35%), with the top two each gaining 1pp, inside the 2pp margin. The tightening only shows up if the ruler is swapped mid-measurement, comparing today's PoderData with yesterday's AtlasIntel, which gave 9.1pp. That is a house effect, not movement, and the panel does not add the two together. For the third time in seven days the price moves a full point without the polling evidence following. The panel records the pattern and does not assert cause, because it has no clear triggering event to attribute it to.
inss.text3: The market on impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice FELL 0.25pp to 3.10% (vol USD 83,000), undoing part of the previous day's 0.55pp rise. Here the point is size, not direction: 0.55pp up and 0.25pp down across two sessions, in a book of USD 83,000 against USD 116.58M in the presidential market, is noise. The day carried real institutional accumulation, with the PT filing at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) a petition of more than 200 pages against a network of profiles using artificial intelligence, and the price went the OTHER WAY. That, by itself, says nothing: in a book that size, direction does not carry enough weight to become a reading.
inss.text4: Two thin books moved a lot today and both deserve the same caveat. In the Senate, the PL FELL 5.50pp, from 71.00% to 65.50%, and the MDB rose 0.60pp, to 18.20%, in a market totalling USD 292,000, with USD 258,000 concentrated in the PL contract itself. In inflation, the modal band is still 5.00% to 5.49%, at 38.30%, but the 4.50% to 4.99% band fell from 34.90% to 32.50% and the 5.50% to 5.99% band rose from 4.10% to 5.80%, in a book of USD 81,000 that is NOT covered by the double-reading capture guard. A large move in a small book is a record, not a signal, and the panel writes the numbers without turning them into a reading.
inss.impactoLula: A new reading, and it comes with two opposite signals in the same week. PoderData/Aya of Jul 30 (field Jul 26 to 29, n=2,400, telephone, 2pp margin, BR-07845/2026) has Lula's personal approval at 43% against 49% disapproval, down 3pp and up 2pp against the institute's own Jul 22 round, and the GOVERNMENT rating at 44% against 50%. Twenty-four hours earlier, AtlasIntel of Jul 29 (n=5,021, 1pp margin) measured 47.6% against 51.2%, with approval RISING 1.7pp against its own Jul 1 round. The two houses therefore point in opposite directions on the same kind of question, in the same week. The panel keeps showing AtlasIntel on the gauge, by the criterion it published on Jul 29, the largest sample and the smallest margin in the window, and records PoderData here without arbitrating which is right. Adding up the week's readings, Lula's approval sits in a band between 43% and 49%, wider than the 47% to 49% band the panel recorded yesterday, and it is PoderData that widens it from below.
inss.impactoGestao: Here is the round's harshest number. On the GOVERNMENT MANAGEMENT rating, which is a different question from personal approval, PoderData of Jul 30 brings 34% good or very good, 16% fair and 47% poor or terrible, with poor or terrible up 10pp against the institute's Jul 22 round. It is a big jump for two weeks. AtlasIntel of Jul 29 measured 49.3% poor or terrible, BTG/Nexus of Jul 27 measured 43% and Datafolha of Jul 24 measured 38%. PoderData's 47% level sits inside that band; what draws attention is the SIZE of the jump inside the house itself. The four institutes still agree on what matters most here: management is rated worse than the person, and the distance between the two indicators persists.
inss.conclusao: With 66 days to the election, the day repeats Jul 28. The favourite's price rose 1.00pp, returned to 63.50% and tied the top of the AFOS series for the third time without exceeding it, with the gap widening to +39.55pp, 0.25pp below the maximum. And the day's polling, read inside the house itself, is flat. The comparison that counts is PoderData against itself, and there the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) gap did NOT move: it was 6pp on Jul 16 (40% to 34%) and it is 6pp now (41% to 35%), with the top two each gaining 1pp, inside the 2pp margin. The tightening only shows up if the ruler is swapped mid-measurement, comparing today's PoderData with yesterday's AtlasIntel, which gave 9.1pp. That is a house effect, not movement, and the panel does not add the two together. What changed in the round was not voting intention, it was evaluation: personal approval at 43%, management with 47% poor or terrible, up 10pp, and rejection TIED at 49% for Lula and for Flávio, when yesterday AtlasIntel gave 49.4% against 52.9%. The asymmetry the panel had been calling a structural constraint on Flávio's candidacy did not show up in this reading, and one round does not undo the series, but it is on the record. The panel does not claim the price rose because of anything: there is no clear triggering event in the day, and three full-point moves in seven days with no matching polling is a pattern the panel would rather record than explain.

bancoMaster.text1: Thursday brought the biggest development in the Master case since the inquiry was opened, and it reaches the campaign directly. The Federal Police is CONSIDERING asking Interpol to include Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro in what is known as a silver notice, an instrument used to locate assets and funds abroad and which is NOT an arrest order, unlike a red notice. The stated aim is to trace the money behind the film Dark Horse, about Jair Bolsonaro's career, which is said to have received R$ 61 million from Vorcaro's Banco Master. The verb matters and the panel will not force it: the Federal Police is CONSIDERING, it has not filed the request, and Interpol has decided nothing (O Globo, InfoMoney, Gazeta do Povo, Jul 30). The measure rests on the inquiry opened on Jul 23 by André Mendonça and, according to the reporting, was prompted by audio released by The Intercept Brasil in which Jair Bolsonaro's son presses Vorcaro for funds earmarked for the film.
bancoMaster.text2: On the legislative front, the news is still the absence of a decision. The writ of mandamus disputing the installation of the Banco Master CPI has sat for more than four months in Kassio Nunes Marques's chambers, and the request by four senators to remove him from the case was rejected. With the Senate in recess and the August agenda still contested between Alcolumbre and the government, there is no deadline in sight. The panel records the elapsed time because it is the fact: four months without a decision on installing a CPI is, in itself, a decision about installing it.
bancoMaster.text3: On price, the record comes with the exact number and with the caveat ahead of the reading: the market on impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice FELL 0.25pp to 3.10%, in a book of USD 83,000. Yesterday it had risen 0.55pp. Across two sessions, therefore, the net move is 0.30pp up, and in a volume that size that is noise. The panel does NOT attribute the move to any specific event, and underlines that the day carried relevant institutional accumulation in the OPPOSITE direction to the price, with the PT filing at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) a petition against a network of profiles using artificial intelligence. When the accumulation and the price point in different directions in a small book, the honest reading is that the book is not big enough to answer the accumulation.
bancoMaster.conclusao: The three fronts of the Master case remain on separate tracks and should not be added together, but on Thursday the criminal one reached the campaign. The Federal Police is CONSIDERING asking Interpol to include Flávio Bolsonaro and Vorcaro in a silver notice to trace abroad the money behind the film Dark Horse, and PT members of Congress asked the Federal Police to investigate alleged favouritism by Flávio towards Vorcaro's bank (O Globo, Jul 30). The asset front remains in the Rio courts, with freezes, and the legislative one remains stalled for more than four months in Kassio Nunes Marques's chambers. The only market touching the case, impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice, pulled back 0.25pp and stands at 3.10%, in a book of USD 83,000 that cannot support a reading of risk repricing in either direction, and which on Thursday moved in the OPPOSITE direction to the institutional accumulation.

stf.toffoli: Toffoli remains isolated at the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) after the Master crisis, with no fresh individual act captured on Thursday.
stf.moraes: No new order from Moraes captured on Thursday. The front he opened is still live: on Jul 28 he gave Jair Bolsonaro's defence 48 hours to explain the video generated by artificial intelligence carrying the former president's image and voice, setting out TWO mutually exclusive hypotheses, and on Jul 29 the defence replied that he did NOT authorize the use of his own image, adding that it does not object to relatives producing that kind of content, a practice it called well known and continuous. It is a defence against breach of precautionary measures, and its effect is to shift exposure from the father to the son and to the party, by way of the deep fake barred under electoral law. The deadline Moraes set has expired and the panel is waiting for the next decision.
stf.gilmar: No individual act by Gilmar in the period. The recent joint vote stands, with Dino, Moraes and Zanin, which eased restrictions on [penduricalhos](/en/glossary#penduricalhos).
stf.dino: No new act on Thursday. Still running is the 10-day deadline he set on Jul 29 for the government and Congress to specify the responsibility of members of Congress over parliamentary earmarks, with the signal that a legislator can be punished for failing to oversee an earmark they themselves designated.
stf.mendonca: He remains rapporteur of the inquiry opened on Jul 23 into Vorcaro's transfers for the film about Jair Bolsonaro, and it is that inquiry which underpins the day's development: the Federal Police is CONSIDERING asking Interpol to include Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro in a silver notice, which locates assets abroad and is not an arrest order. The Federal Police is considering, it has not filed the request, and Interpol has decided nothing (O Globo, InfoMoney, Gazeta do Povo, Jul 30). On the overseas asset tracing already authorized, the two corrections of record still hold: the decision was signed in MAY and only became public on Jul 28, and the reporting stopped being single-sourced as of Jul 29.
stf.nexo: Thursday's connecting thread is the same as the two previous days, artificial intelligence in campaigning, but this time the move came from a PARTY and not from a justice. The Brazil of Hope Federation, which brings together PT, PCdoB and PV, filed at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) a petition of more than 200 pages against a network of 31 profiles that, ACCORDING TO THE FEDERATION'S CLAIM, uses artificial intelligence to attack Lula. The figures in the petition, all attributed to the federation and not independently verified by the panel, are 1,464,245 combined followers, 23,828 posts and an estimated reach of 10 million accounts, with boosting attributed to Flávio Bolsonaro and other politicians. The requests are for removal of URLs, lifting the anonymity of those responsible and suspension of monetization (Metrópoles, CNN Brasil, Migalhas). It is the third consecutive day in which the panel's institutional axis is the use of artificial intelligence in campaigning, and the structural novelty is that the dispute is no longer only between the STF and a defence: a party is now the petitioner at the TSE.
stf.analise: The market on impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice before 2027 FELL 0.25pp to 3.10% (vol USD 83,000), undoing part of yesterday's 0.55pp rise. The methodological caveat comes before the reading and it is the usual one: 0.25pp in a book of USD 83,000, against USD 116.58M in the presidential market, is very little money, and does not license talk of risk repricing in either direction. With the caveat made, what matters is the MISMATCH. The day carried relevant institutional accumulation, with a party filing at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) a petition of more than 200 pages on the use of artificial intelligence in campaigning, and the price went the other way. On Jul 29 the panel recorded the price direction following the accumulation; today it contradicts it. Two days, two directions, a net move of 0.30pp up. The honest reading is that this book is not big enough to respond to institutional news, and that trying to read cause into it in either direction would be building narrative on noise. The panel records the numbers and stops there.
